content.name: Kendra Whitfield
content.title: Mathematics Department Chair and High School Math Teacher
content.summary: National Board Certified math teacher with 16 years in North Carolina public high schools, now chairing a 14-teacher math department. My AP Calculus AB pass rate has stayed above 80% for six years, and I led the shift to a co-taught Math I model that raised end-of-course proficiency by 17 points.

experience.title: Mathematics Teacher
bullets: Taught Math I, Math II and Honors Precalculus to 5 sections of about 28 students each.
Started a free after-school tutoring lab staffed by National Honor Society students, serving 70 students a week.
Raised the share of my Math I students scoring proficient on the end-of-course exam from 52% to 68% in three years.

experience.title: AP Calculus and Precalculus Teacher
bullets: Grew AP Calculus AB enrollment from 2 sections to 5 by recruiting underrepresented students through a summer bridge course.
Kept my AP Calculus AB pass rate (score 3+) between 79% and 88% across five exam years.
Mentored 5 beginning teachers through North Carolina's beginning teacher support program.
Earned National Board Certification in Mathematics/Adolescence and Young Adulthood in 2017.

experience.title: Instructional Coach, Secondary Mathematics
bullets: Coached 22 math teachers across 4 high schools using observation cycles, co-planning and model lessons.
Designed a district remote-learning math toolkit during school closures, used by 90+ teachers.
Helped write a common Math I curriculum map and assessments, adopted districtwide in 2021.

experience.title: Mathematics Department Chair and AP Calculus Teacher
bullets: Lead a 14-teacher math department, setting course sequences, PLC agendas and a $31,000 annual materials budget.
Launched co-taught Math I sections with the special education team, raising end-of-course proficiency from 41% to 58%.
Secured a $24,000 local education foundation grant for graphing calculators and a data science elective.
Teach 3 sections of AP Calculus AB and keep the department's AP pass rate above 80%.
